story: The Church Street Marketplace is an uncovered outdoor pedestrian shopping and dining mall made of four blocks of Church Street, between Main and Pearl streets. The idea for it began in 1958 as part of urban renewal discussions.

In the summer of 1971, a one-day street fair on the four blocks drew about 15,000 people. A week-long fair followed in 1972, with traffic rerouted to the parallel streets. The mall was built in 1980 and 1981 to a design by Carr, Lynch Associates of Cambridge, Massachusetts.
It has about 86 storefronts. The American Planning Association named it one of America's Great Public Spaces for 2008.
stops.fact: A one-day street fair in 1971 helped prove the mall could work.
stops.disputed: Many people think the mall was an overnight decision. Wikipedia says it took from 1958 to 1981, with trial street fairs along the way.

claims.t: The Church Street Marketplace was built in 1980 and 1981.

claims.why: Wikipedia says the idea began in 1958.

story: Battery Park is a public park overlooking Lake Champlain at the western end of downtown Burlington. It was named for the artillery that American forces stationed there during the War of 1812.

On August 13, 1813, American gunners, helped by the USS President, defended the position against an attack by a British squadron led by Lt Colonel John Murray. The park land was deeded to the City of Burlington in 1870.

The park has a bandshell, a playground and monuments, including a bronze statue of Civil War veteran General William W. Wells and a red oak sculpture of Chief Gray Lock. It is a popular place to watch fireworks on the Fourth of July.
stops.fact: The park was deeded to Burlington in 1870.
stops.disputed: Many people repeat that Rudyard Kipling called this one of the two finest sunset views in the world. Wikipedia reports it only as 'according to' Kipling, so treat it as a claim, not a record.

claims.t: Battery Park was named for artillery stationed here.
The park land was deeded to the city in 1972.
claims.why: Wikipedia says 1870. A 1972 extension was added to the south end.

story: Old Mill, historically known as the Main College Building, is the oldest campus building of the University of Vermont. The first Main College was built in 1801 and 1802 by John Johnson, but it burned down in 1824. Johnson also designed its replacement.

The cornerstone for North College was laid on April 26, 1825 by Vermont Governor Cornelius P. Van Ness. Two months later, on June 29, General Lafayette laid the cornerstone for South College during his tour. A third building, Middle College, was added in 1829.

Each of the buildings was built 7 to 8 feet apart to keep a fire from destroying the whole thing again. They were connected in 1846. The building was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1975, as part of the University Green Historic District.
stops.fact: The buildings were built 7 to 8 feet apart to stop a fire from spreading.
stops.disputed: Many people hear the name 'Old Mill' and think it ground grain. Wikipedia says it was the Main College Building.

claims.t: The first Main College building burned down in 1824.
claims.why: Wikipedia: its predecessor burned down in 1824.

claims.t: The Old Mill building was a grain mill.
claims.why: Wikipedia says it was historically called the Main College Building.

story: Billings Memorial Library was built in 1883 and designed by the American architect Henry Hobson Richardson to resemble the Winn Library in Woburn, Massachusetts. Frederick H. Billings of Woodstock donated it to the University of Vermont.
It opened in 1885 and was a central part of campus life. In 1961 the university built a new library because Billings was too small, and in 1963 the old one became a student center.

After the Davis Center opened in 2007 as the new student center, Billings got an $11.4 million renovation that finished in 2018. It is home to academic departments again, including Special Collections.
stops.fact: The building has been a library, a student center and then academic offices.
stops.disputed: Many people think a building keeps one job for life. Wikipedia says Billings was a library, then a student center from 1963, then academic space after 2018.

claims.t: It has been used only as a library.
claims.why: Wikipedia says it was a student center from 1963.
